title: Recent Inflation Developments and Challenges for Research and Monetary Policymaking
summary: Loretta Mester, President and CEO of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland, delivered a speech at the Konstanz Seminar discussing inflation dynamics across major central banks in 2015-2016. The speech reviews the FOMC's 2% PCE inflation target (established January 2012), notes that U.S. inflation ran at 0.66% (2015), below the Euro area (0.25%) and UK (0.20%), and identifies weak global demand, energy price declines, and dollar appreciation as common disinflationary factors. Mester emphasizes the importance of understanding inflation measurement, forecasting, and transmission mechanisms for monetary policy, and explicitly states these are her own views and not necessarily those of the Federal Reserve System or FOMC colleagues.
key_points: The FOMC's explicit 2% inflation target (PCE) was established in January 2012 and reaffirmed as symmetric—concern warranted if inflation runs persistently above or below target
2015 inflation prints: U.S. 0.66% (PCE), Euro area 0.25% (HICP), UK 0.20% (CPI)—all well below respective targets
Common disinflationary factors cited: weak global demand post-financial crisis, declining energy/commodity prices, and dollar appreciation
Fed staff SIGMA model: 10% real dollar appreciation reduces core inflation by ~0.5% within one year, partially reversing thereafter; also reduces GDP with a lag
Mester explicitly states views are her own, not necessarily those of the Federal Reserve System or FOMC colleagues
Historical context: deflation during Great Depression 1930s; inflation surged in 1970s until Volcker's contractionary policies caused early-1980s recession
why_it_matters: The speech provides insight into how a regional Fed President framed the low-inflation puzzle circa 2016. It documents the empirical fact that major central banks were undershooting targets simultaneously and identifies transmission channels (import prices via dollar appreciation, commodity prices, demand) that remain relevant for understanding disinflation. While not policy prescriptive, it reflects the intellectual framework of a future Cleveland Fed President who would serve until 2024.
macro_context: This speech discusses macro conditions from 2015-2016 when inflation was below target across major economies. It identifies three key disinflationary forces: weak post-crisis demand, declining energy/commodity prices, and dollar appreciation. The speech contextualizes the FOMC's symmetric 2% inflation target (reaffirmed annually as symmetric by the Committee) and notes that inflation has been a persistent focus since the Great Recession. Fed staff SIGMA model estimates that a 10% real dollar appreciation reduces core inflation by ~0.5% within one year. Historical examples of missed price stability (1930s deflation, 1970s-80s inflation under Volcker) are cited to emphasize the importance of central bank vigilance.

~0.5% — core inflation impact one year after 10% dollar appreciation shock
